title: Claude Tackles AMD Chip Low-Level Adaptation in Just 3 Days: NVIDIA CUDA's Moat Faces Its Strongest Challenge Yet
excerpt: The competitive landscape of AI hardware and the underlying software ecosystem is undergoing a profound structural shift. Recently, major industry news emerged:
content_html:
The competitive landscape of AI hardware and the underlying software ecosystem is undergoing a profound structural shift. Recently, major industry news emerged: Anthropic's Claude Mythos reportedly took only 3 days, with almost no human intervention, to successfully complete nearly 100% of the low-level kernel code for the AMD MI355X chip.

This breakthrough directly reduced a chip adaptation cycle that would normally require dozens of senior engineers and take 6 to 12 months to just 72 hours. In actual tests, the performance gap between the ported model and Nvidia's CUDA-optimized solution was only 8% to 12%, which already fully meets the standards for commercial deployment.

Cross-Chip Barriers Drop Sharply, Compute Supply Chain Ushers in a Diversified Shift

For a long time, Nvidia has been able to dominate the AI compute market not simply because of its chip hardware performance, but because of the moat around its CUDA software ecosystem, built over many years and stacked up by countless engineers writing code. For other chipmakers, the high adaptation costs and long software porting cycles have long been an insurmountable gap.

This time, Claude's extremely high efficiency in writing low-level code has torn a hole in Nvidia's software barrier and greatly lowered the threshold for cross-chip adaptation. Based on this technical progress, Anthropic has now reached a compute supply partnership with AMD for up to 2 gigawatts.

Advantages and Limitations Coexist: Multi-GPU Collaboration Remains the Future Focus

Although this technological breakthrough has caused widespread shock in the industry, many analyses have remained objective and rational.

From the perspective of use cases, the breakthrough currently mainly covers the inference prefill stage. In highly difficult areas such as multi-GPU collaboration for ultra-large-scale distributed training, Nvidia still maintains a clear lead thanks to its deep technical accumulation. Therefore, this progress has not completely overturned the CUDA ecosystem landscape in a short time, but it has undoubtedly introduced uncertainty into the entire compute market and is accelerating the global compute industry toward a more open and diversified direction.
